title: Tenant-aware headroom reconciler: predictive target metric reconciliation, fairness, and emergency backoff
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a reconciler in the autoscaling policy engine that produces per-tenant and per-model scaling targets by combining short-term predictive demand, configured latency SLO mappings, and fairness adjustments. The reconciler must: 1) convert heterogeneous signals (tokens/sec, QPS, concurrent requests, queue length, p95/p99 latency) into a single effective throughput target; 2) respect reserved capacity and tenant-level fairness constraints; 3) enforce safety limits (rate-of-change, budget guard, min/max capacity); and 4) provide deterministic fallbacks and emergency backoff when predictor or metric streams are degraded.
acceptance_criteria: Reconciler computes a single target throughput (tokens/sec or instances) for each tenant-model pair and surfaces it to the scaler API
Targets respect tenant reserved capacity and fairness weight such that aggregate guaranteed capacity is never violated under normal operation
Scaling decisions do not exceed configured rate-of-change limits (no more than 30% delta per minute by default) unless in emergency backoff
End-to-end simulation demonstrates stable behavior across five representative workload traces (startup spike, diurnal, bursty tails, steady QPS, degraded telemetry)
Observability: dashboards show target vs actual, reasons (predictor, latency, fairness), and safety limit hits; alert if predictor is down and fallback used
design_notes: Overview: The reconciler runs every control interval (default 10s) and executes three stages: (A) Predictive Demand Estimation, (B) Metric Reconciliation to target units, (C) Fairness & Safety Adjustment. Predictive Demand Estimation uses short-window weighted exponential smoothing on tokens/sec and request arrival rates; optionally a light-weight ML predictor (XGBoost-lite) can be enabled per-customer. Metric Reconciliation maps latency SLOs to implied throughput using an empirically calibrated latency-throughput curve per model (stored in model profile). Formula (informal): effective_target = max(predicted_tokens, throughput_from_latency_SLO, queue_based_target). throughput_from_latency_SLO = inverse_latency_curve(SLO_latency, current_seq_len_distribution). Safety and fairness are applied as multiplicative adjustments: final_target = clamp(fairness_weight * effective_target, min_reserved, max_budget). Reconciler must annotate decisions with reason codes ("PREDICTOR", "SLO_MAP", "QUEUE", "FALLBACK") for tracing.
scaling_algorithms: Discrete stepper with decaying credit pool: convert target delta into discrete instance scale-ups with fractional credit carryover
Model-aware bin-packing: prefer colocated model variants to reduce KV cache miss amplification when scaling nodes
Emergency backoff: if predictor fails or p95/p99 exceed hard thresholds, immediately cap new accepts to safe_headroom and throttle non-critical tenants
Soft-proportional split: when multiple tenants contend for burstable pool, allocate based on configured fairness_weight and recent usage quotas
safety_limits: min_replicas per tenant-model: from reserved_capacity (cannot scale below)
max_replicas per tenant-model: configurable hard cap (default 200 instances)
cooldown_window: 120s after a scale event before allowing another full-size scale (partial adjustments allowed)
cost_budget_guard: daily spend cap per tenant that prevents further scale-ups when breached (soft alarm then hard block)
emergency_safety_fence: if global p99_latency > X ms AND telemetry degraded, trigger conservative fallback that uses reserved capacity only
rollout_steps: Spike-test in staging with 3 synthetic tenants using representative model mixes
A/B canary on 5% of dedicated fleet: reconciler ON vs baseline for 24h, compare cost, tail latency, and scale churn
Enable per-tenant opt-in flags; gather feedback from two anchor customers
Progressive ramp to 50% then 100% after SLO verification; include automatic rollback on safety condition
Post-rollout: 1-week monitoring window and a follow-up retrospective to tune default rate-of-change and fairness weights
test_plan: Unit tests for mapping functions and reason-code production
Deterministic simulator running 1000-day equivalent traces with random spike injection to validate stability
Integration tests: metrics pipeline degradation, predictor failure, reserved capacity enforcement
Chaos test: introduce delayed telemetry and ensure emergency backoff engages and recovers gracefully
Load test: ensure reconciler compute is sub-ms per tenant at 10k tenants (scale benchmarking)
